title: MethodX: constant fan-in DST with dynamic neuron ablation
method: MethodX: sparse-to-sparse dynamic sparse training with a constant fan-in constraint (every active neuron has exactly k incoming weights). Every ΔT steps, per layer: count each neuron's salient weights (layer top-K by weight or by gradient magnitude), ablate neurons with fewer than γ_sal·k salient weights (floor of one) and give their budget to the rest, recompute k′, prune the K smallest-magnitude weights layer-wide, and regrow each active neuron by gradient magnitude up to fan-in k′. ERK (or uniform) layer densities, sparse fan-in-scaled init, update fraction α cosine-decayed to zero at an end fraction, then the mask is frozen. Inference uses a condensed n_active × k values + indices representation with CPU and GPU kernels; a closed-form variance analysis of the output-norm ratio motivates the constraint.

compute.hardware: Training pool 4× A100 for 6 weeks (to be confirmed before S0; if V100s, ≈1,613 A100-h); V100 latency box and Xeon CPU separate from the training budget

outOfScope.item: Fine-tuning or transfer from pretrained models

outOfScope.reason: needs a truly sparse training implementation, a separate engineering project; C6 is stated as algorithmic sparsity only

claims.text: MethodX learns constant fan-in sparsity with sparse-to-sparse training; it is equivalent to RigL and non-inferior to GraNet up to very high sparsity, across ResNet, WRN, MobileNetV2 and ViT/DeiT
At very high sparsity unstructured DST implicitly ablates neurons; strict constant fan-in prevents this, and dynamic ablation restores accuracy because it makes width compatible with the constraint
Neuron ablation can be enabled at all sparsities; the resulting width sparsity adds inference speed without hurting generalization
The condensed representation is parameter- and memory-efficient and gives real speedups for batch-1 CPU and batched GPU inference compared with dense and with strong unstructured engines
Constant fan-in does not impair training dynamics: output-norm variance is no larger than unstructured, especially at high sparsity
Training is algorithmically fully sparse: sparse weights and optimizer state, and sparse forward/backward except for the dense gradient at update steps (no training wall-clock speedup claimed)
On CIFAR, MethodX generalizes better than post-hoc constant fan-in projection and better than SR-STE N:M learning at equal sparsity
Hardware N:M supports only one fixed ratio and uniform sparsity

questions.text: On R18/C100 and WRN-22-2/C10 (sparsity 80→90→95→98→99) and R50/IN (90→95→99), is MethodX top-1 equivalent to RigL (paired TOST, 90% CI inside ±δ) and non-inferior to GraNet (one-sided 95% lower bound > −δ) at each sparsity? The claimed range s* is the last sparsity passed before the first failure (fixed-sequence, ascending).
questions.hypothesis: s* ≥ 98% on both CIFAR architectures and s* = 99% on R50/IN
questions.predictionIfFalse: s* < 95% on any of the three; the 'very high sparsity' wording is dropped if s* < 98% on CIFAR or s* < 99% on ImageNet (a 99% failure caused only by a CI wider than δ is reported as inconclusive)

questions.text: Does the Q1 equivalence vs RigL hold on MobileNetV2/C100 and ViT-Tiny/C100 at {90, 95, 98}% (fixed-sequence), and on DeiT-S/IN at 90%?
questions.hypothesis: s* ≥ 95% on MobileNetV2 and ViT-Tiny, and equivalence holds on DeiT-S at 90%
questions.predictionIfFalse: Equivalence fails at 90% on any of them; C1 is narrowed to the families that pass and the failing family is reported as a limitation

questions.text: Does RigL implicitly ablate neurons, does strict constant fan-in lose accuracy at the highest sparsity, and is width compatibility the mechanism (width-oracle, RigL+abl, one-shot vs dynamic)?
questions.hypothesis: (a) RigL's zero-fan-in fraction rises with sparsity and is ≥ 5% at 99%; (b) strict is ≥ 1.0 pp worse than MethodX at the highest sparsity of each architecture (99% R18, WRN, R50/IN; 98% MobileNetV2); (c) the width-oracle recovers ≥ 75% of the strict→MethodX gap; (d) RigL+abl changes RigL by less than δ; (e) dynamic ablation beats one-shot at init by ≥ δ at 99%
questions.predictionIfFalse: Strict-vs-MethodX difference < 0.5 pp everywhere, or RigL ablates < 1% of neurons, or the width-oracle recovers < 25%; if RigL+abl ≥ RigL + δ, C2 is reworded (ablation is partly a general improvement); if one-shot is within δ of dynamic, report that one-shot suffices

questions.text: Does a high-γ_sal setting remove many neurons at non-inferior accuracy, and does deleting ablated neurons speed up the same trained weights?
questions.hypothesis: On R18/C100 the val-selected high-γ_sal setting from A2 removes ≥ 10% of neurons at 90% sparsity; it is non-inferior to default MethodX (5 paired seeds, one-sided 95% lower bound > −δ) at 90% and 95%; on the same trained weights condensed+deleted runs ≥ 1.1× faster than condensed with zero rows, CI lower bound > 1.0
questions.predictionIfFalse: Non-inferiority fails, or the same-weights speedup is < 1.05×

questions.text: Is batch-1 CPU latency of the condensed model faster than dense (oneDNN/MKL) and than the best unstructured engine per layer (MKL inspector-executor CSR, XNNPACK sparse, torch.sparse CSR, same-toolchain CSR), on the same weights?
questions.hypothesis: Speedup ≥ 1.2× vs dense and vs the best unstructured engine at ≥ 90%, with the 95% bootstrap CI lower bound > 1.0

questions.text: Same question on V100 at batch {1, 8, 64, 256} vs cuBLAS dense, cuSPARSE CSR, Sputnik and a same-toolchain (Triton) CSR kernel
Does the analytic output-norm variance match Monte Carlo, and is constant fan-in no worse than unstructured in variance and static training?
questions.hypothesis: Analytic variance of ‖z^{l+1}‖²/‖z^l‖² matches MC within 5% relative error; Var(constant fan-in) ≤ Var(exact-count) ≤ Var(Bernoulli) at all tested sparsities; static random constant fan-in is no worse than static unstructured by more than δ
questions.predictionIfFalse: Var(constant fan-in) > Var(Bernoulli) beyond MC error at any sparsity ≥ 90%, or static constant fan-in is worse by more than δ

questions.text: Training cost of the sparse algorithm: theoretical training FLOPs and analytic training memory, plus measured masked-implementation step time and peak training memory (MethodX vs RigL vs dense)

On R18/C100 and WRN/C10 at 90 and 98%, does MethodX beat post-hoc constant fan-in projection, SR-STE and Chase (95% CI of the paired difference excludes 0 and |diff| ≥ the minimum effect; Holm over 12)?

decisionPoints.if: costs overrun (ImageNet/DeiT per-run costs beyond 1.37× the planning values, or the projected finish is late)
decisionPoints.then: apply the cut ladder in order: (1) C3; (2) R50/IN 80% points; (3) M4 and M6 dense → published numbers; (4) M-GN 99% → copied for context; (5) M3 95% → 1 seed, indicative; (6) drop M5 DeiT-S

decisionPoints.if: calibrated costs are at or below plan and the projected finish is ≤ day 38
decisionPoints.then: apply the restore ladder: (1) A8 + A9; (2) DeiT-S 95%, MethodX and RigL, 1 seed each; (3) Chase R50/IN 90%, 1 seed, context

decisionPoints.if: the training pool turns out to be V100s (≈1,613 A100-h)
decisionPoints.then: V100 rescope: keep S0, S1.1, S1.4, T-IN, T-arch, T0 on an 8-config grid, M1, M2 without secondary baselines, M-MB, M-ViT without the attention variant, M7, R50/IN MethodX and RigL at {90, 99} × 3, A1-IN, A1, A1-W, P1, P3, RA, P2, A2 at {90, 99} + A2-Q4, C4; drop DeiT-S, GraNet on ImageNet, ImageNet 80/95%, ImageNet dense, C3, A3–A7, A10 (1,608 with reserve)

decisionPoints.if: the static floor is not ≥ 1 pp below RigL at 90% on val
decisionPoints.then: shift the sparsity grid to {95, 98, 99, 99.5}

decisionPoints.if: C0: condensed is slower than the alternatives (< 1.0×) at 95% on random masks
decisionPoints.then: rescope C4 now to the regime where it wins and prioritize kernel work before S4

decisionPoints.if: a sanity gate fails
decisionPoints.then: debug with at most 2 attempts; if RigL is still off by more than 0.5 pp, switch both arms to the official RigL code or report the gap explicitly

decisionPoints.if: G1: the upper bound of (MethodX − RigL) is < −δ at 90% or 95%
decisionPoints.then: rewrite C1 as 'within X pp'; restrict R50/IN to {90, 99}; cancel M5/M6; no MethodX-only retuning

decisionPoints.if: G2: the upper bound of (MethodX − strict) is < 0.5 pp at both 98% and 99%
decisionPoints.then: cut P1, P3 and RA (75 GPU-h to reserve); A1-IN still runs and decides C2

decisionPoints.if: G3: RigL's zero-fan-in fraction is < 1% at 99%
decisionPoints.then: drop the C2 mechanism claim; cut P1 and P3; keep RA

decisionPoints.if: G4: analytic variance is more than 5% from MC
decisionPoints.then: fix the derivation before P2

decisionPoints.if: G5: the upper bound of the ViT (MethodX − RigL) gap is < −δ at 90%
decisionPoints.then: release M5/M6 (700 GPU-h) to the restore ladder; report the transformer failure as a limitation

decisionPoints.if: G6: MethodX − RigL at 99% on minival is < −2.0 pp (1 seed)
decisionPoints.then: cap ImageNet C1 at 95%; still run the M3 99% seeds for A1-IN pairing

decisionPoints.if: G6: the code hash is unchanged after S1.5
decisionPoints.then: reuse the S1.5 runs as M3 seed 0

decisionPoints.if: the selected high γ_sal for C3 equals the default
decisionPoints.then: skip C3

decisionPoints.if: C2 decision: strict-vs-MethodX is ≥ 1.0 pp with Holm significance on ≥ 3 of 4 architectures including R50/IN
decisionPoints.then: keep the C2 claim
decisionPoints.else: rewrite C2 descriptively, with no causal claim

decisionPoints.if: P1 recovery: the width-oracle recovers < 25% of the gap
decisionPoints.then: width is not the mechanism (25–75% is reported as partial)

decisionPoints.if: RA: RA ≥ RigL + δ
decisionPoints.then: reword C2: ablation is partly a general gain

decisionPoints.if: γ_sal sensitivity: the accuracy range across γ_sal at 95% exceeds 2 pp

decisionPoints.if: speed gate: speedup < 1.2× or CI lower bound ≤ 1 vs dense or the best unstructured engine
